item.text:
**Bottom Line**
Mixed, leaning no. I found some real technocratic capacity-building in regulatory agencies, but no direct 2024 evidence that Hasina systematically empowered competent economic professionals at the top of economic decision-making. The stronger pattern in the record is politicized, prestige-driven, or patronage-prone governance in major spending choices.

**Accepted Claims**
- [Bangladesh: remarkable development progress](https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099514001022413953) — World Bank, December 31, 2023, disclosed January 2, 2024.  
  Claim: Bangladesh entered 2024 with substantial development gains already in place, including lower-middle-income status, gender parity in school enrollment, and major mortality reductions. This is the best broad positive background evidence that the state had at least some competent development capacity, though it does not show who was appointed or empowered in 2024.  
  Question IDs: `5B.2`, also `5B.1`

- [Bangladesh reaffirms commitment to nuclear non-proliferation and peaceful use](https://www.dhakatribune.com/bangladesh/foreign-affairs/345281/bangladesh-reaffirms-commitment-to-nuclear-non-proliferation-peaceful-use) — Dhaka Tribune, April 30, 2024.  
  Claim: The foreign minister said Bangladesh would maintain high transparency, safety, and security for its nuclear plants and highlighted IAEA support for training and capacity building. This is positive, but it is indirect evidence of technocratic empowerment in a specialized regulatory area, not direct proof about economic ministries.  
  Question IDs: `5B.2`, also `5B.1`

- [Bangladesh nuclear regulators train at Russia's Novovoronezh NPP](https://www.neimagazine.com/news/bangladesh-nuclear-regulators-train-at-russias-novovoronezh-npp/) — Nuclear Engineering International, June 18, 2024.  
  Claim: BAERA inspectors were trained with Russian regulator support, and this was the fourth group of specialists to receive such training. This supports the existence of a technical pipeline rather than pure loyalist staffing, but it is still sector-specific.  
  Question IDs: `5B.2`, also `5B.1`

- [Rooppur Power Plant: 48 Bangladeshi specialists complete pre-licensing training](https://dailycountrytodaybd.com/story/rooppur-nuclear-power-plant-%3A-48-bangladeshi-specialists-complete-pre-licensing-training) — Daily Country Today, July 8, 2024.  
  Claim: Forty-eight specialists completed pre-licensing training and still had to obtain BAERA licenses. That is a concrete competence-and-licensing pipeline, which is the kind of institutional discipline this lens looks for.  
  Question IDs: `5B.2`, also `5B.1`

- [Bangladesh creates second Rooppur plant request](https://www.thedailystar.net/news/bangladesh/news/consider-setting-2nd-nuclear-power-plant-3580751) — The Daily Star / UNB, April 2, 2024.  
  Claim: Hasina asked Rosatom to consider a second Rooppur plant and directed formalities for taking back spent fuel. This shows some operational attention to custody and back-end management, but it is not evidence of broad technocratic empowerment across the economy.  
  Question IDs: `5B.2`, also `5B.1`

- [Bangladesh's nuclear prestige illusion](https://www.thedailystar.net/opinion/views/news/bangladeshs-nuclear-prestige-illusion-3590666) — The Daily Star, April 20, 2024.  
  Claim: This opinion piece argued the second-plant push looked prestige-driven amid debt and inflation. That is negative evidence that major decisions were being shaped by image and politics rather than by professional economic judgment.  
  Question IDs: `5B.2`, also `5B.1`

- [Rooppur cost inflation and politically linked contracts](https://en.banglaoutlook.org/news/1099) — Bangla Outlook, April 23, 2024.  
  Claim: The article alleged major cost inflation and politically linked ancillary contracts around Rooppur. If accurate, this points toward patronage and weak discipline rather than empowered, independent economic professionals.  
  Question IDs: `5B.2`, also `5B.1`

- [Rooppur Power Plant was AL govt's white elephant, energy sector experts](https://www.tbsnews.net/bangladesh/energy/rooppur-power-plant-was-al-govts-white-elephant-energy-sector-experts-958801) — TBS News, October 5, 2024.  
  Claim: Energy-sector experts described Rooppur as a white-elephant project tied to mismanagement and corruption under the Awami League government. This is strong negative evidence against a clean technocratic-governance story.  
  Question IDs: `5B.2`, also `5B.1`, `4B.4`, `4B.5`

**Search Gap**
- I found no direct 2024 evidence showing Hasina specifically appointed competent economic professionals to top economic posts, or that she purged loyalists/family/business-linked figures from those roles.
- The strongest positive evidence is indirect and sectoral: technical training, licensing, and IAEA-backed capacity building in the nuclear regulator.
- The strongest negative evidence is governance style: prestige, patronage allegations, and white-elephant/mismanagement criticism around major projects.
